My ephemeral stint with Wellsite contract ended yesterday. Can’t use their proprietary products and build proprietary solutions. This is the third or fourth company whom I have refused to work for because of my free/libre open source philosophy advocacy. It makes me wonder what have I contributed to the free software movement so far. When I speak of contribution I usually refer to software work - programming, testing, documentation and so on. I have refused to work a person who wanted Emacs customization before just because the code was privately hosted. What I see here with this recent contract agreement was:

  • I failed to negotiate initially for free software licensing of my work
  • Also, not being vocal about my beliefs and philosophy. Pragmatism, unfortunately hasn’t been my strengths. It may be difficult for me to proceed along the lines of business using a free software philosophy

Not sure whether I want to earn money through paid work for a profit making business.

Spent time earlier forwarding SlashDot stories to BNR. A waste of my time. Unnecessary - I don’t need to repay his debts of sending me some information or teaching or recommendation. Needless. Pointless. Moved the Libreboot laptop from the small portable desk to the keyboard drawer of the larger desk. It should be okay for now to use it from here. The only problem being the length of the DisplayPort cable - the keyboard/machine cannot be fully drawn out from drawer to type characters.

A quarrel with P and now here I am out in the open at the dreaded co-working space. Trying to blow my hard earned money at flimsy things. An utter waste of my time. Everyday begins with a rant. The same mundane rant. Repetitious and perpetual it continues. Trying to use the space for free? I belong nowhere. Not in the corporate, not at home, not on streets, not on mountains, not in a village, nowhere. Nowhere.
